summary: The abstract cap in consensus JSON is a serialization concern, not an engine one: every gate and classifier reads the full reconstructed abstract, so the capped output must stay opt-out-able or the JSON cannot be used to audit what the engine actually decided.
reason: The relevance gate, the PICO gate and ClassifyStance all consume scWork.Abstract in full; clipAbstract runs afterwards, only while building workBrief. That gap makes the emitted JSON unfaithful as an audit trail — a study can be excluded on text the consumer never receives, and replaying a gate over the emitted corpus produces exclusions that never happened in production. A regen must keep the cap defaulted ON (bounded LLM prompts is why it exists) while leaving an explicit way to turn it off.
validated_outcome: Measured on 12 archived corpora before the flag existed: 110 of 246 studies (45%) reached the consumer already truncated, and replaying the current PICO gate over coffee's own survivors excluded a work that had passed at runtime. clipAbstract is proven byte-identical to its pre-flag implementation across empty/at-cap/over-cap/multi-byte inputs while the flag is off.
